correctness.rationale: Expand y^c by marking an arbitrary subset with weight t per mark. For either pattern compare suffix and prefix standardizations: shifts 1 and 2 disagree, and shifts 3 and 4 agree. At shift 4 the old maximum is shared as the next minimum and the four new values lie above it. At shift 3 in 12435 the second shared value is the old maximum and all three new letters are larger; in 13245 the two shared positions contain the top two of the latest occurrence. They are the top two of the whole chain inductively (true initially, preserved by either extension). The new rank-2 letter inserts between them, and ranks 4 and 5 append above them. This gives exactly one total order per compatible chain signature. The last value strictly increases along each overlapping gap, excluding a fully closed marked chain. A sole mark has a gap n≥5 back to itself. Cutting at every gap ≥5 gives disjoint chains, possibly touching at gap 5, and singleton uncovered positions, each in a canonical atom. For length n and k atoms, distinguish one of the k atom boundaries in an indexed configuration. This gives a linear ordered tuple of k atoms starting there and a choice of its starting index among n options; conversely these data give the distinguished boundary in the indexed configuration. Therefore the contribution of A^k is multiplied by n/k, even for rotationally periodic words. The singleton-only configurations handle the empty marking and n<5; for a<5 the expression reduces to ze_1/(1−ze_1). Substitution t=y−1 restores ordinary occurrence weights, and coefficient symmetry gives content-permutation stability.
residual_risks: Frozen replay path is python3 verification/cyclic_patterns_check.py; its 447,720 word instances and 126 finite chain cases are recorded corroboration, not an all-length proof. The code was inspected, not independently executed.

evidence: The two relevant primary results split the necessary features: repeated-letter linear cluster constraints versus distinct-entry circular enumeration. Li's abstract explicitly includes 12435 among its linear examples.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Linear cluster weights can be reused, but they are not alone enough: one has to exclude a marked configuration wrapping as a single unsplittable chain and count indexed atom cycles with stabilizers correctly. The distinct-entry logarithmic identity cannot specify coefficients containing powers x_i^b for b>1 by specialization; identifying distinct labels may change whether a window meets the strict distinctness rule. The comparison does not rule out an uninspected general cyclic-cluster theorem.

evidence: Chen–Fang–Kitaev analyze linear multiset permutations. Elizalde–Sagan use circular permutations of distinct entries modulo rotation. Reverse-complement takes 12435 to 13245 but reverses content coordinates.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Reverse-complement alone gives equality across reversed contents, not equality within each content, and passage from linear to cyclic changes the positions where occurrences are tested. Indexed and unindexed distinct-entry counts can be converted by a factor of n; with repeats and nontrivial stabilizers this is not an equivalent enumeration.

value.rationale: The result resolves all counts by multiplicities and number of occurrences, including wraparound, for explicit nonmonotone patterns. The total-order property makes each connected contribution a single elementary symmetric function rather than a general order enumerator, and the proof isolates exactly the additional condition needed to use cyclic atoms. This yields useful exact distribution and stability information in a domain not handled by distinct-entry circular enumeration.
residual_risks: No necklace formula or general all-pattern cyclic stability classification is established.
